title: Fidelity Budget Scheduler and Sweep Catalog
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document specifies the Fidelity Budget Scheduler (FBS) and a canonical sweep catalog used by Applied ML to run reproducible, cost-aware evaluation sweeps across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. FBS translates business/engineering priorities and monetary/token budgets into concrete eval-harness jobs with fidelity profiles, quantization constraints, and scheduling SLAs.

Scope: covers policy, fidelity bands, scheduling heuristics, operational runbook for failed/slow sweeps, CLI examples, and integration notes for the eval-orch and probe-farm services. Does NOT prescribe model-specific metrics or threshold values — those belong in the model onboarding acceptance matrix.

Motivation

- We run many sweep types: smoke checks, stability regressions, quantized regressions, adversarial probes, and large coverage sweeps. Each has different cost and timeliness requirements.
- Teams have limited eval budgets; FBS ensures predictable spend and repeatable coverage by mapping "budget bands" to fidelity profiles and resource classes.
- FBS reduces ad-hoc eval sprawl, decreases wasted compute on low-value probes, and creates repeatable signals for rollouts and regressions.

Definitions

- Sweep: a collection of eval jobs for a given prompt set, split into slices.
- Fidelity Profile: a named set of evaluation knobs (seeds, candidate counts, adversarial augmentation, multi-turn depth).
- Budget Band: a named cost/time envelope (micro, small, full, extended).
- Eval-orch: the internal orchestrator that schedules eval-harness jobs against probe-farm compute pools.

Components

1) Fidelity Profiles (canonical):
   - low-fidelity: single-seed, 1 candidate, deterministic sampling; used for quick smoke checks and CI gating.
   - medium-fidelity: 3 seeds, top-3 candidates, light adversarial probes on high-priority slices.
   - high-fidelity: 5+ seeds, diverse sampling, adversarial/randomized perturbations, multi-turn chaining for stateful workloads.
   - quant-check: medium fidelity but forces quantization profile matrix (int8, int8+KV, float16) and records per-slice degradation metrics.

2) Budget Bands

| Budget Band | Walltime target | Max evals (approx) | Typical use-cases | Default fidelity | Default pool |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| micro | < 1 hour | <= 50 | CI smoke, pre-commit checks | low-fidelity | shared-cpu |
| small | < 6 hours | <= 500 | Quick regression triage, PR-level checks | medium-fidelity | burst-gpu-small |
| full | < 48 hours | <= 10,000 | Release readiness, model promotion, SLA regression | high-fidelity | dedicated-gpu |
| extended | <= 7 days | <= 100k | Large-scale stability scans, multi-model ensembles | high-fidelity + extended adversarial | multi-cluster |

3) Quant Constraints
   - Sweeps that include quant-check must list allowed quant profiles in the sweep manifest and must also register a control non-quantized run.
   - Default quant profiles: int8, int8-kv, float16. For private deployments set via quant-profile-override in onboarding manifest.

Scheduling Policies

- Priority Tiers: low (background), normal (developer-triggered), high (release block). Priority determines preemption and fair-share on probe-farm.
- Admission Control: Eval-orch subjects each sweep to a cost estimate step; if the estimated compute/token cost exceeds the project's monthly budget remainder, the sweep is queued to low-priority or rejected with an explanatory error.
- Prefetching / Warmup: For full/extended bands, probe-farm reserves KV caches for models that benefit from warm-up; the scheduler charges a fixed warmup credit to the sweep budget.
- Adaptive Throttling: If latency SLOs (see Operational SLOs) are at risk, scheduler will throttle medium fidelity sweeps by reducing seeds or candidate counts automatically. This change is recorded and tagged as "fidelity-throttled" in telemetry.

Operational SLOs and Alerts

- Completion SLO: 90% of small-band sweeps should complete within the band walltime; 95% for micro.
- Cost SLO: per-sweep estimated cost should be within ±20% of final billed cost 90% of the time.
- Noise SLO: quant-check sweeps must have per-slice variance < 8% relative to non-quantized baseline or flag for manual review.

Alerting rules (examples):
- alert_eval_sweep_stalled: fired if a sweep reports no job progress for 60 minutes and has > 5 running tasks. Pager to eng-platform team.
- alert_quant_degradation: fired if quant-check variance exceeds Noise SLO on >= 3 high-priority slices. Send email to model-onboarding owners and applied-ml oncall.

Runbook: Common Procedures

1) Submit a new sweep (owner: evaluator / applied-ml engineer)\   
   1.1 Create sweep manifest (YAML) with: name, prompt-set, slices-file (s3://), budget-band, fidelity-profile, quant-profiles (optional), related-release-id.
   1.2 Run local cost estimate: `redwood-eval estimate --manifest sweep.yaml` and confirm.
   1.3 Submit: `redwood-eval run --manifest sweep.yaml` or via eval-orch UI.
\2) Sweep stuck in queued state > 2h (owner: eng-platform oncall)\   
   2.1 Check eval-orch logs: `kubectl logs deploy/eval-orch -n evals --since=2h`.
   2.2 Check probe-farm pool usage: `probe-farmctl pool-status`.
   2.3 If blocked by budget, inform owner and suggest lowering fidelity or scheduling off-peak window.
\3) Quant-check failure (owner: applied-ml / model owner)\   
   3.1 Review per-slice reports in S3 (path printed in sweep metadata).
   3.2 If degradation crosses thresholds, mark the model version as QUANT-RISK and open a regression triage ticket using template `quant-regression-template` with links to artifacts.

Triage Playbook for Regression Signals

- Initial signal: failing slices from high-fidelity sweep or a spike in error-rate in production telemetry mapped to eval slices.
- Fast path: run a targeted small-band sweep using the failing slice set with quant-check and an unquantized baseline; if the failure reproduces, escalate to causal-regression team and attach sweep manifest and job ids.
- Bisect: use the automated-regression-bisect assistant (see related_pages) to isolate commit/manifest changes.

CLI Examples

1) Micro smoke sweep\

```
redwood-eval run --name smoke-latest --prompt-set s3://prompts/smoke.yaml --budget-band micro --fidelity low-fidelity
```

2) Quant-aware small sweep\

```
redwood-eval run --name quant-check-salesbot --prompt-set s3://prompts/salesbot/slices.csv --budget-band small --fidelity quant-check --quant-profiles int8,int8-kv
```

Kubernetes job snippet (simplified)

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: eval-sweep-quant-check
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: eval-runner
        image: registry.redwood.internal/eval-runner:stable
        args: ["--manifest", "/manifests/sweep.yaml"]
      restartPolicy: Never

Integration Notes

- Link to evaluator-sdk adapters: sweeps must use the standard evaluator-interchange-format (see evaluator-interchange-format doc) so downstream analysis and dashboards can aggregate metrics.
- For Private deployments: the sweep manifest must include `data-plane: private` and quant-profile overrides must be declared. Onboarding checklist requires a smoke-run on a staging cluster before production sweeps.

Acceptance Criteria for Promoting a Sweep Template to the Catalog

- Reproducibility: template produces the same top-level slice pass/fail on 3 independent runs within tolerance.
- Cost estimate accuracy: final cost within 20% of estimate for >= 5 historical runs.
- Observability: per-slice telemetry, logging, and artifact retention metadata present in manifest.

Appendix A — Sweep Manifest (example)

```yaml
name: "salesbot-quant-check-2026-02"
prompt_set: "s3://prompts/salesbot/primary.yaml"
slices_file: "s3://prompts/salesbot/slices.csv"
budget_band: "small"
fidelity_profile: "quant-check"
quant_profiles: ["int8","int8-kv"]
related_release: "release-2026-03"
retention_days: 30
```

Appendix B — Mapping to Eval-harness Jobs

- The scheduler expands the manifest into groups of eval-harness jobs by slice shard. Each job is labeled with `sweep=<name>`, `band=<band>`, `fidelity=<profile>` and writes artifacts to `s3://eval-artifacts/<team>/<sweep-name>/<job-id>/`.

Notes and Future Work

- Planned: automated fidelity annealing (start high-fidelity on critical slices, automatically degrade non-orthogonal slices after X% progress to save budget).
- Investigate: per-tenant cost attribution so teams can be auto-billed for extended sweeps.

Ownership

- Product steward: Applied ML (eval orchestration)
- Implementation: eng-platform (eval-orch, probe-farm)
- Oncall / Triage: applied-ml oncall for model regressions; eng-platform oncall for scheduling/infra issues.
